waterMl.notes: No change from FitPlate general water target; low HDL and metabolic syndrome alone do not change water needs. Drink more in heat, exercise or fever per general rules. Many people with metabolic syndrome take BP medicines, including water pills (diuretics), so the app shows only the general range and never pushes a higher target. Choose water, plain chaas and unsweetened drinks; avoid sweet chai, soft drinks, packaged juice, sharbat and alcohol. Follow your doctor's advice.

warnings: General information, not medical advice. FitPlate does not diagnose low HDL or metabolic syndrome; a clinical assessment and blood tests by a doctor are needed.
The app never suggests starting, stopping or changing any medicine or supplement (statins, fibrates, niacin, metformin, BP medicines, omega-3 capsules). Follow your doctor.
Do not take niacin or fish-oil capsules to raise HDL on your own; large trials of niacin added to statins showed no benefit and the HDL-raising approach is not recommended in a review.
HDL can fall with sugar-heavy and refined-carbohydrate diets, excess weight, inactivity and smoking; a higher HDL from alcohol is not a reason to drink (WHO: no safe level).
Very high HDL is not a goal; a Danish cohort found higher all-cause mortality at extreme HDL values.
Metabolic syndrome means several risk factors together; raised BP, glucose or triglycerides each need their own review; TG of 500 mg/dL or more: see P5 and talk to your doctor.
Emergency: chest pain, sudden breathlessness, or stroke signs (face droop, arm weakness, speech difficulty). Seek emergency care now (112).
With heart, kidney or liver disease, pregnancy or diuretics, follow your doctor's advice on fluids.

requires_doctor_input is true because metabolic syndrome bundles raised BP, glucose and triglycerides that often need medicines and monitoring, and many users take diuretics or other BP medicines; the app sets only general food, weight, activity, alcohol and sodium guidance on its own.
